exposure: Umbilical artery half peak systolic velocity deceleration time (hPSV-DT) value (< 5th percentile vs. >= 5th percentile)
cohort: The study included pregnant women with preeclampsia at 28-41 weeks gestational age admitted to the Department of Perinatology.
finding: Umbilical artery hPSV-DT was successful in predicting composite adverse perinatal outcomes, including NICU admission, RDS, and low birth weight, in pregnant women with preeclampsia, showing better predictive ability than UA-PI.
followup_time: Neonatal period, covering outcomes like APGAR scores, NICU admission, and RDS.
birth_weight: Birth weight was measured as an outcome, with a threshold of < 2500 g also considered an outcome; no specific inclusion criterion for birth weight was applied.
gest_age: Mothers were between 28-41 weeks gestational age at admission, and gestational age at birth was measured as an outcome for the babies.
